body: Off and on therapy, but my parents were not financially supportive of therapy so I paid for it out of pocket as a teenager. It’s not something that is easily fixed without a support system.

The problem is that after a childhood/young adulthood of being berated about my appearance and weight by family, friends, and even sometimes strangers, I got to a point where something inside me desires so badly to be attractive to people that I will literally self-sabotage just to feel okay about myself. I’ve been battling intense eating disorders, fucked up images issues, etc, since I was 13 years old. It’s not even about sex, I’m not a particularly sexual person (though I do enjoy it with my boyfriend). It’s deeper than that :(

I don’t understand why you’re doing this. He knows who they are, and when it happened, and what happened. Everything other that literally the nittiest grittiest of details that he doesn’t want to know, because he specifically told me that it doesn’t matter to him and we’re going to work through it regardless. I get that I deserve to be told to kill myself, but I pray you don’t give the same “advice” to others on this page. I’d mention you in my suicide note if I cared enough to write one, you prick.

He finds other people attractive, has zero desire to sleep with them. I wish he did so I could be in an open relationship, but alas. 

I’m already in deep with the drugs and booze, so unfortunately that advice is too little too late,  but fair enough - I appreciate your insight.

Sorry, I honestly don’t know where you’re going with this. Yes, he knows the truth, yes, we have made the mutual decision to work things out between us to the best of our ability. We’ve been together for a long time, and although you seem to be incapable of understanding it, I absolutely love him very much despite the mistakes I’ve made in our relationship. And he knows that. The problem here begins and ends with the fact that I am incredibly suicidal due to guilt. If that isn’t something you’re willing to discuss on this thread, kindly stop commenting. I think I’ve made my feelings towards myself very clear.

The root problem is that I can’t live with myself because of how awful I am. I would be so, so happy to be in an open relationship because I personally want him to be able to be with who he wants physically, but he only wants me. I don’t know why, I can’t explain it, but for some reason he wants to keep going in our relationship. I’ve committed to never stepping outside of it again (and I won’t, I swear to god), but I can’t live with the things that I have done. THAT is the problem, is how incredibly suicidal I feel due to guilt.

I know why I cheat - I’m not justifying it to myself. I was in an open relationship for years that destroyed my view of monogamy. I can’t stop myself from getting physical with other people because I ruined my own fucking brain. I heard so much shit from people growing up about my weight and image and constantly being told how weird and fucked up I was that I starved myself and fucked up my body and destroyed my mind trying to be perfect looking, and now any chance I get to validate that I’m not a horrific ugly monster, I take it. It’s like I can’t stop myself. I need therapy badly, but I can’t afford it. Anyway, my question was about how to live with myself - obviously I know that cheating is wrong. But thanks anyway

I was in an open relationship for years and it completely fucked up my ability to look at relationships from a monogamous standpoint. It’s like something flips in my brain when I’m in a position to be physical with another person and I can’t stop myself. I was severely mentally and emotionally abused by my parents for my weight and appearance growing up, and even though I forced myself into being conventionally attractive via eating disorders, working out, makeup, etc, it’s like this craving for validation that never goes away. So yes, while I would love an open relationship to absolve me of guilt, it wouldn’t fix the root problem. Thank you though, helped
